newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Share power or face new Bosnia war, Bildt warns.
newsitem.headline: Share power or face new Bosnia war, Bildt warns.

text.p: Carl Bildt, the international peace coordinator in Bosnia, warned on Monday that a refusal by nationalists to share power after Saturday's elections would mean a new war.

"If we don't implement the constitution (prescribed by the 1995 Dayton peace treaty), we are lost, and so is peace," Bildt told a news conference focusing on preparations for the fraught elections and the precarious period afterwards.

Bildt, the international High Representative in Bosnia, laid out a timetable for creating joint Moslem-Serb-Croat governing bodies after the elections, devised to reunify Bosnia after the division along ethnic nationalist lines in the war.
Over the past months, the leading parties from each rival ethnic faction have repeatedly broken pledges set out in the Dayton documents, which established the framework for national reconciliation.

All factions have blocked refugees from crossing former front lines to return to their homes, there have been widespread reports of intimidation of opposition politicians, and leading politicians frequently resort to nationalist rhetoric in their campaigns.
Human rights groups warn there is no real freedom of movement, no freedom of association and no freedom of the press -- all essential elements of democracy and the Dayton accord.
Ruling nationalist Serbs in particular say their intention is to win independence for their Bosnian Serb Republic carved out by war, rather than reunify the country as the peace accord demands.
At the news conference, Bildt was repeatedly challenged as to how he could expect the factions to share power now after having flouted the Dayton agreement so far.
Bildt responded that the Moslem-Croat and Serb entities in Bosnia would have considerable autonomy under a multi-ethnic presidency and House of Representatives.
"Bosnia will be the most decentralised state in existence in the world," he said. "If power-sharing does not work, peace will not last."
But outside powers were determined to make it work and had drafted a package of strong "incentives and disincentives" to help make recalcitrant factions comply.
